ral phosphoric acid (CPA)-catalyzed 1,8-addition of indolizines to propargylic alcohols. This strategy achieves enantioselective and re-
gioselective C1-functionalization of indolizines under mild reaction conditions with low catalyst loading, broad functional group toler-
ance (35 examples), and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 96% ee). Moreover, the scale-up reaction and late-stage C3-function-
alizations demonstrated its potential applications. DFT calculations were carried out to clarify the reaction mechanism and the origin
of enantio- and regioselective control.

Background and Originality Content
Axially chiral allenes are important structural motifs common-
ly found in natural products,<sup>[1]</sup> pharmaceuticals,<sup>[2]</sup> and chiral cata-
lysts or ligands (Figure 1a).<sup>[3]</sup> Consequently, numerous methods
for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral allenes have been
developed,<sup>[4]</sup> primarily including direct functionalization of al-
lenes,<sup>[5]</sup> conversion of prochiral

and isomerization of
alkynes.<sup>[7]</sup> However, most of the established approaches focus on
synthesizing 1,3-di- or trisubstituted chiral allenes. Very recently,
organocatalytic
or 1,8-conjugate addition<sup>[9]</sup> of propargylic
alcohol has been demonstrated as a powerful method for the
construction of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes. Despite these ad-
vances, driven by the persistent challenges in accessing chiral
tetrasubstituted allenes formation, the development of new cata-
lytic enantioselective approaches is still highly valuable and de-
sirable.

and indolizine moiety.
On the other hand, indolizines have garnered increasing at-
tention due to their distinctive structural features and unique
properties, which render them highly promising for biomedical
and fluorescence applications (Figure 1b).<sup>[10]</sup> As a result, extensive
efforts have been devoted to synthesizing structurally diverse
indolizines over the past decades.<sup>[11]</sup> In recent years, the direct
functionalization of indolizines has emerged as an efficient syn-
thetic route for modifying indolizine moieties and attracted con-
siderable attention. Among these, several attractive C3-function-
alizations of indolizines have been reported in this field, including
C‒H activation,<sup>[12]</sup> propargylation,<sup>[13]</sup> Lewis acid catalysis,<sup>[14]</sup> visi-
ble-light or electro-induced,<sup>[15]</sup> as well as organocatalytic 1,4-con-
jugate addition (Scheme 1a).<sup>[16]</sup> In sharp contrast to the well-de-
veloped C3-functionalization of indolizine, the direct and regiose-
lective C1-functionalization of indolizine remains challenging and
elusive, especially for the C3-unsubstituted derivatives. Very

recently, only very few reports concerned on the regioselective
and enantioselective C1-functionalizations of indolizines through
Mannich reaction.<sup>[17]</sup> Our group also successfully disclosed a CPA-
catalyzed regio- and enantioselective C1-arylation of β,γ-alkynyl-
α-imino esters with pyrrolo[2,1-a]isoquinolines.<sup>[18]</sup> Building upon
these results, we became interested in this promising asymmetric
C1-functionalization of indolizine via remote 1,8-conjugate addi-

selective 1,6- or 1,8-conjugate addition of propargylic-para-qui-

reaction site without hydrogen bonding involvement.

of our methodology.

(DFT) calculations were systematically performed. The reaction
pathway begins with the dehydration of substrate 1a catalyzed by
chiral phosphonic acid (CPA), leading to the formation of key in-
termediate I1. Subsequently, substrate 2a approaches I1 under
the stereocontrol of CPA, where two competitive pathways
emerge: (1) the kinetically favored 1,8-addition proceeding
through transition state TS1 with a Gibbs free energy barrier of
15.1 kcal/mol to afford product 3aa; and (2) the thermodynami-
cally controlled 1,6-addition via transition state TS1' with a higher
barrier of 18.5 kcal/mol, yielding regioisomer 4aa. Notably, an

Conclusions
In conclusion, we have successfully established a CPA-cata-
lyzed 1,8-conjugate addition of propargylic alcohols with indoliz-
ines, enabling direct access to axially chiral tetrasubstituted al-
lenes via remote stereocontrolled C1-functionalization. This
strategy addresses the long-standing challenge of regioselective
C1-attack on indolizines, featuring mild conditions, low catalyst
loading, broad substrate scope with high regio- and enantiocon-
trol. The reaction scalability and late-stage derivatization demon-
strated their potential as versatile chiral building blocks. Mecha-
nistic studies and DFT calculations confirm a kinetically favored
C1-attack pathway, providing insights for future asymmetric de-
sign.
